patches.scope_notes: Chronic-disease prevention and population-health practice, including surveillance/survey and GIS analyses, evaluation and systematic reviews. Scoping reviews are excluded from the systematic-review category. The methods label maps to practical instructional Tools for Public Health Practice articles, which require a one-paragraph summary to the editor before manuscript submission; it does not establish a generic algorithm-paper format. Current guidance says submitted data should be the most current and no older than two years. CDC states that its publications must comply with Executive Orders 14151 and 14168; the editor may discuss identified concerns with the corresponding author. General information: https://www.cdc.gov/pcd/for_authors/general_information.htm.

findings.issue: Authorship by experts worldwide does not explicitly affirm universal geographic eligibility; instructions also include editorial review for executive-order compliance.
findings.resolution: Changed author eligibility to not_stated and added the official research-content condition to scope notes.

findings.issue: Journal instructions list research conduct, data collection and interpretation but do not specifically name generated code.
findings.resolution: Retained conditional compatibility under the campaign interpretation of human-responsible code-assisted analysis, explicitly marking the inference and retaining disclosure requirements.

findings.issue: Official policy expressly discusses AI in data collection and analysis and writing assistance, but does not name generated code.
findings.resolution: Retained conditional compatibility as code-assisted data analysis, an interpretation, with methods and separate writing disclosure.

findings.issue: Official policy contemplates AI text generation, data analysis and other research components; code is not separately named. No separate comprehensive page or membership cost evidence.
findings.resolution: Retained qualified conditional compatibility and needs_verification fee route; code-assisted analysis is an interpretation.

findings.issue: Current journal editorial policy was inaccessible to the AI auditor, and journal location evidence is historical.
findings.resolution: Retained unclear AI compatibility and venue location caveat; no inference of current AI permission.

findings.issue: Five printed pages are free, but charges apply above that threshold; Sage policy has a generation restriction.
findings.resolution: Retained explicit page limit and unclear AI classification, without claiming that long submissions are free or that drafting is permitted.

notes: Reviewed all 17 baseline and discovery records against all three completed fee, geography and AI helper patches, including routes, restrictions, location evidence and compatibility. Independently read official PAHO author instructions via direct HTTPS after web tool 403; SciELO RESS policy; CDC PCD author, editorial and about pages; Bulgarian journal official ethics PDF; and OUP European Journal of Public Health metric page. Other helper evidence was evaluated from its recorded claims rather than independently refetched in every case.

Preserved all pre-existing dated and clearly labeled historical/undated metrics; official 2025 European Journal 5.2 JIF and 4.8 CiteScore confirmed, as was PCD 2025 JIF 5.6. No extra acceptance estimate invented. Citation measures do not predict manuscript acceptance.

AI analysis/code for RESS and Bulgarian journal reflects code-assisted work within expressly contemplated data analysis, not explicit named permission for arbitrary code generation; PAHO research-conduct language supports a similarly bounded interpretation. Human verification and the relevant disclosure requirements apply.

These are agent evidence reviews, not human scientific review. Fee waivers, optional OA, special supplements and scope constraints remain as recorded by the fee and geography auditors. No remote actions performed.
